answer.text: Short-term money-market instrument with maturity up to one year

explanation.text: The Logic: Commercial Paper is a money-market instrument with a maturity up to one year. It is short-term in nature and trades alongside other money-market instruments. The Trap: Long-term bonds, equity and preferred stock are different instrument classes with materially different cash-flow and tenor profiles. Note: Money-market instruments include CP, Certificates of Deposit and Treasury Bills; all are short-tenor by definition.
